title: Stakeholder alignment, retrospective & contingency facilitator script
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a facilitator-first script and slide outline for a 90-minute customer session focused on aligning cross-functional stakeholders at the midpoint of a POC. The goal: surface gaps, lock in decisions for deployment cutover, and rehearse contingency plans so we can avoid last-minute escalations. Use for customers who are moving from prototype to pilot, especially when multiple teams (product, infra, legal, security) have outstanding concerns.

Outcome we want by end of session:
- Single list of open decisions with owners and due dates.
- Agreed deployment window and rollback triggers.
- Prioritized risk register and mitigations.
- 3 immediate next actions assigned (engineering, security, customer success).

Attendees (recommended roles):
- Customer: Product PM, Eng lead, Security architect, Ops lead
- Redwood: Solutions Eng facilitator (owner), Embedded SE, Customer Success Manager, SRE representative (if Dedicated/Private)

Pre-reads (send 48h before):
- Current POC runbook (link)
- Short recording of last demo (2–3 slides)
- Minimal architecture diagram (1 page)

Timing and flow (90 minutes):
1) 0:00–0:05 — Welcome & objectives (Facilitator)
   Script: "Thanks everyone, quick round of intros. Today we’ll focus on three things: align on outstanding decisions, finalize a deployment contingency plan, and agree next steps for the cutover. We’ll capture owners and due dates live."

2) 0:05–0:20 — Quick POC health pulse (all)
   Slide: POC health dashboard (latency, error rate, cost burn, key feature coverage)
   Facilitator prompt: "One-sentence pulse from each team: green/yellow/red and why."

3) 0:20–0:40 — Open-decision mapping (breakout or round-robin)
   Slide: Decision matrix (Decision | Impact | Options | Owner | Due Date)
   Activity: For each outstanding decision, capture options and a recommended default. Assign owner and decision date.
   Script for SE: "We recommend option A because ... if there are objections, note them and we’ll add mitigation items."

4) 0:40–0:60 — Deployment contingency workshop (whole group)
   Slide: Contingency play cards (Rollback, Degraded Mode, Model Fallback, Region Failover, Ops Escalation)
   Facilitator exercise: Walkthrough the most likely failure scenarios (pick top 3 from risk list). For each: trigger conditions, responsible team, immediate steps, escalation path, metrics to monitor.
   Prompt: "If latency exceeds X or error rate > Y for 5m, we execute fallback plan B and page on-call SRE."

5) 0:60–0:80 — Runbook dry-run / communications plan
   Slide: Runbook excerpt (who says what to whom) + sample Slack and pager messages
   Activity: Read aloud the first 3 messages, confirm channel ownership and on-call numbers.

6) 0:80–0:85 — Parking lot / unresolved items capture
   Slide: Parking lot (questions for offline)

7) 0:85–0:90 — Commitments & next steps (Facilitator)
   Slide: Summary of owners/dates + immediate next 72h tasks
   Script: "Restate the three highest priority actions and owners. We will publish minutes and a revised runbook within 24 hours."

Slide deck outline (10–12 slides):
- Title + objectives + expected outcomes (1 slide)
- Who’s in the room / roles & pre-reads (1 slide)
- POC health dashboard (1 slide)
- Outstanding decisions matrix (1–2 slides)
- Top risks and short rationale (1 slide)
- Contingency play cards (1 slide)
- Example runbook snippets & communication templates (1 slide)
- Dry-run checklist (1 slide)
- Commitments and owners (1 slide)
- Annex: links to artifacts, logs, test data (1 slide)

Facilitator tips and scripting notes:
- Keep time tightly observable — call out 2-minute warnings. Use a visible timer.
- Normalize tradeoffs: "We’re choosing the safer option given the cutover window; we can iterate post-launch."
- When tensions rise, reframe as a testable hypothesis and create a short experiment: "Can we validate X in 24h?"
- Use parking lot liberally to avoid tangents; capture and assign.

Breakout exercise templates (if splitting into two groups):
- Group A (Decision owners): Build a mini decision memo (1 slide): what we pick, why, rollback option, monitoring.
- Group B (Ops & SRE): Draft a 5-step contingency checklist and the first Slack pager line.
Provide 12 minutes, then 4 minutes for group reports.

Contingency examples (ready-to-copy):
- Model fallback: If token generation latency > 2s p50 for 3 consecutive minutes, route to smaller quantized model variant. Notify engineering and decrease batch size.
- Region failover: If 95th percentile latency increases by 30% and sustained errors > 2% for 10m, reroute traffic to secondary region and initiate postmortem.
- Data visibility issue: If request traces drop below 90% sampling or logs show missing request IDs, escalate to infra within 30 minutes.

Post-session deliverables (owner, due):
- Revised runbook + decision ledger (Solutions Eng, 24h)
- Updated deployment checklist and play cards (SRE, 48h)
- Follow-up technical deep-dive for security concerns (Security architect + Redwood SE, 72h)

Success metrics to track after session (short window):
- All open decisions resolved or assigned within 48h
- Runbook published and acknowledged by attendees within 24h
- No unplanned rollbacks during first 7-day pilot (target)

Prep checklist for facilitator (24–48h out):
- Confirm attendee list and roles; escalate if key decision-maker missing
- Load slides and demo environment; test screen share and video
- Prepare a one-page architecture cheat-sheet for quick reference
- Pre-populate decision matrix with known items to save time

Common failure modes and mitigation (for facilitator awareness):
- Failure: dominant voice blocks decisions. Mitigation: use dot-vote or quick straw poll.
- Failure: too many technical deep dives. Mitigation: capture action item and ask for a 20–30m follow-up call.
- Failure: ambiguous owners. Mitigation: require owner name + backup + due date for every item.

Notes and loose thoughts (parking lot for the facilitator):
- Consider shipping an annotated runbook with sample logs so customer knows what to look for during cutover.
- Add a short A/B fallback test earlier in POC to reduce final-week risk.
- Offer a 2-hour scoped on-call shadow during first business-day of pilot as optional add-on.

Document history:
- 2024-11-07 created by Aisha Patel
- 2024-11-10 edits: added contingency play cards and post-session deliverables (Marco Rivera)

End of doc.
